root_cause.text: ext4’s unwritten-extent split path incorrectly treated “split before submitting I/O” like a real extent conversion by passing EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT into ext4_split_convert_extents(), which could partially convert the on-disk extent to written while leaving the extent-status tree unwritten on ENOSPC and expose stale data later.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `flags | EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` from `ext4_ext_handle_unwritten_extents()` when `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_SPLIT_NOMERGE` is used, and changes `ext4_split_convert_extents()` to only set `EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2` for actual convert-to-initialized cases; the CVE text explains that with `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` set, `ext4_split_extent_at()` may fail with `-ENOSPC`, zero only the first half, convert the whole on-disk extent to written, but leave the second half unwritten in the extent status tree, allowing stale data exposure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ext4 unwritten-extent splitting so conversion to initialized data is only applied for explicit convert requests.
intent_record.what: In ext4_split_convert_extents(), the conditional handling was changed so that the branch for splitting an existing unwritten extent now triggers when either EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_UNWRIT_EXT or EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT is set. Within that branch, EXT4_EXT_MARK_UNWRIT2 is always set, while EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 is now set only when EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT is present. The comment was also updated to distinguish "Split the existing unwritten extent" from "Convert to initialized".
intent_record.how: This changes extent-splitting behavior for unwritten extents: requests to split an unwritten extent can now be handled without necessarily converting the split-off part to initialized data. Only explicit convert operations mark the second part as valid initialized data, while pure unwritten-extent split requests preserve unwritten semantics. This avoids applying initialized-data handling in cases that should remain unwritten.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop unconditionally passing EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT when splitting unwritten extents so the conversion path uses the intended flags.
intent_record.what: In the call to ext4_split_convert_extents(), the fifth argument was changed from `flags | EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` to պարզապես `flags`; the surrounding indentation was adjusted accordingly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ext4_split_convert_extents() now receives the original flag set without forcibly adding EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT for this path, which changes the extent-splitting/conversion behavior in the SPLIT_NOMERGE case.

This call site invokes the split-convert helper for the unwritten-extent path; combined with the unconditional conversion flag, it triggers the flawed conversion semantics that can leave stale data exposed.
